query: For a selected high-entropy alloy whose superconducting behavior remains uncharacterized, what governs whether and how superconductivity emerges in the low-temperature test regime, and why? Propose one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison with the starting state, the observations expected relative to that baseline, the limits over which the hypothesis should hold, supporting prior evidence, and a clear falsification criterion.

generation.hypothesis: In the high-entropy alloy, the high degree of configurational disorder homogenizes the electronic environment, thereby suppressing anisotropic superconducting properties. This results in a superconducting state with lower effective mass anisotropy compared to a structurally more ordered control alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: As-cast high-entropy alloy with high configurational disorder and uncharacterized superconducting behavior.
generation.intervention: Cool the alloy into the superconducting regime and perform angular-dependent resistivity measurements along with an effective mass analysis under varying magnetic field orientations.
generation.conditions: Experiments conducted at temperatures well below the superconducting transition temperature (Tc) in a cryogenic environment, under moderate magnetic fields, with careful rotation of the magnetic field relative to the sample’s principal crystallographic axes.
generation.structural_mediator: High configurational entropy produces a homogeneous distribution of atomic-scale scattering centers, which averages out directional disparities in electron pairing and effective mass.
generation.mechanism: Enhanced electron scattering caused by the random atomic arrangement leads to a reduction in directional variations of the superconducting electron effective mass. This suppressed anisotropy in the electronic system favors an isotropic superconducting pairing state, distinct from that observed in more ordered systems.
generation.predicted_outcome: The high-entropy alloy will exhibit significantly reduced angular variation in resistivity and a lower effective mass anisotropy parameter (γs) compared to a control sample with reduced configurational disorder.
generation.baseline: A similar alloy composition processed to have reduced configurational disorder (e.g., via thermal annealing or using components with lower mixing entropy) that exhibits a higher degree of superconducting anisotropy in angular-dependent resistivity measurements.
generation.boundary: The predicted effect should be observable in the low-temperature superconducting regime under moderate magnetic fields. Near Tc or at fields high enough to suppress superconductivity, the anisotropy differences may become indiscernible.
generation.uncertainty: While the success of angular-dependent resistivity measurements in other layered superconductors supports the approach, the quantitative impact of extreme configurational disorder on effective mass anisotropy in HEAs remains uncertain and may depend on sample preparation and measurement resolution.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of samples: one set of the as-cast high-entropy alloy exhibiting high configurational disorder and one set of control samples with reduced disorder (e.g., via post-casting annealing). Cool both sets below Tc and perform systematic angular-dependent resistivity measurements under a controlled rotating magnetic field.
measurements: Effective mass anisotropy parameter (γs) determined by scaling analysis
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-entropy (disordered) samples show effective mass anisotropy values (γs) statistically similar to or greater than those obtained from the more ordered control samples, the hypothesis that configurational disorder suppresses anisotropy in the superconducting state will be falsified.

By considering the effect of Sc on the crystal structure and microstructure of the senary Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr system, it is instructive to review first the structural and microstructural features of the quinary Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr parent system, which has been studied extensively in literature [,,,,,,,]. The as-cast Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr HEAs of various chemical compositions are fully single-phase, crystallizing in the bcc structure with the lattice parameter in the range a= 3.36–3.37 Å. For some compositions, two bcc phases were detected in the same material, one with a smaller parameter aS≈ 3.36 Å and the other with a larger aL≈ 3.40–3.48 Å. The situation is completely analogous to the bcc phase in the Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys (see Table 3), indicating that the bcc phase fraction in the Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr could be the same as the bcc phase in the Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr parent system. This also suggests that the bcc phase in the Sc-Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys likely does not contain any Sc, i.e., all Sc binds into the hcp phase. reading.lever: Adapt angular-dependent resistivity measurements and effective mass analysis to probe superconducting anisotropy at low temperatures.
reading.why: This approach, successful in elucidating anisotropy in layered superconductors, can directly reveal how high configurational disorder in the HEA governs superconductivity emergence.
